text:
maria_support: Heads-up — customer reported sudden vectors/sec drop on embeddings endpoint, tokens/sec looks normal. Started ~09:12 UTC.

tyler_eng: can you paste the high-level numbers? tokens/sec vs vectors/sec?

maria_support: tokens ~210k/sec (stable). vectors down from ~11.5k/sec to ~2.8k/sec on their steady-state workload. No auth errors, requests 200 OK.

ana_oncall: looks like typical kvcache/batch issue — any dim mismatch logs?

maria_support: I see a couple of warnings in the app logs: "embedding_dim_mismatch expected=1536 got=128 for request id=usr-34f" but only 3 of those. Most requests succeeded but throughput still low.

tyler_eng: can you run a quick probe against our staging embed endpoint with the same payload mix? Repro steps they used?

maria_support: Repro steps from customer: small dense 64-token docs, batch of 64 per request (really many small vectors per request). They sent long tail of tiny inputs. I ran: 

curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"embed-1536","input":["short text","short text",...],"batch_size":64}'

jamie_infra: when you repro, can you capture GPU queue depth metrics (gpu_queue.depth) and kvcache hit ratio?

maria_support: attached quick snapshot from staging during my run: 
- gpu_queue.depth: spiked to 120 during the slowdown
- kvcache.hit_ratio: 12% (normally ~78%)
- avg batch_size: 4.1 tokens/batch (expected ~18)

ops-bot: deploy-notify: autoscaler v2.7.4 rolled out to serving pool 'embed-prod' at 2024-06-11T08:58:14Z.

tyler_eng: ah — autoscaler rollout matches timeframe. Could be autosplit/sample_rate change that shrank batching windows. Is there a config flag named sample_rate?

jamie_infra: yes, v2.7.4 introduced dynamic sample_rate to reduce tail latency: it shortens batch window for high arrival-rate clients. Looks like it undershot for this workload (too aggressive).

simon_ml: that would reduce batch packing and K/V cache reuse -> more GPU kernel overhead per vector, hence vectors/sec drop but tokens/sec (token generation) unaffected because that's different path.

ana_oncall: any temporary mitigation we can push to the customer?

tyler_eng: We can pin them to a fallback model variant (embed-1536-stable) that uses the old batching profile, or we can flip sample_rate back for their tenant. Which is faster?

maria_support: customer wants a quick fix, pinning model variant is easiest. How do we pin from support side?

jamie_infra: I can update routing policy for their tenant to model=embed-1536-stable and set batching.max_window_ms=40 (instead of 12) — that should increase avg batch sizes. Ready to apply after approval.

maria_support: do it. Also share repro script so engineering can run a controlled benchmark.

tyler_eng: I'll run bench with two payload types: many tiny inputs and few large inputs. Command: 

python tools/bench_embeddings.py --host https://staging --model embed-1536 --clients 8 --requests 2000 --payload tiny_list.json

simon_ml: collect perf counters: token_throughput, vector_throughput, gpu_queue.depth, kvcache.hits, batch_size.histo. We need before/after numbers for v2.7.3 vs v2.7.4.

maria_support: jamie applied route pin and batching change at 09:46 UTC. Customer confirms vectors/sec recovered to ~10.8k/sec.

ops-bot: rollout-rollback: sample_rate override applied for tenant acme-inc at 2024-06-11T09:46:27Z by jamie_infra.

ana_oncall: good. Keep monitoring for 30m, capture traces for any 5xxs.

jamie_infra: grabbed flame graphs — before change: avg batch_size 17.6, kvcache.hit_ratio 74%, gpu_queue.depth 28. After change: avg batch_size 4.3, hit_ratio 11%, gpu_queue.depth 125.

tyler_eng: root cause summary: autoscaler v2.7.4 dynamic sample_rate algorithm reduced batching window aggressively for high-arrival tiny-payload clients; this reduced batch packing and kvcache locality causing GPU kernel overhead increase and vectors/sec regression. Tokens/sec unaffected because generation path not impacted by kv-cache for embedding-only inference.

simon_ml: follow-ups: 1) add workload fingerprinting to prevent small-doc heavy tenants from hitting aggressive sample_rate. 2) add automated regression test that runs embed vector throughput microbenchmark during rollout. 3) revert default sample_rate tuning until we have safety checks.

maria_support: customer happy with temporary fix, asked for ETA on permanent fix. Can we provide an ETA?

tyler_eng: patch for sample_rate safety checks + e2e tests — estimate 2 sprints (4 weeks). Hotfix to revert aggressive decision can be done in 2 days if PM signs off.

maria_support: passed to customer: temporary pin applied, sustained throughput back to normal; engineering estimates 2 days for hotfix option or 4 weeks for full safe rollout. They accepted 2-day hotfix.

ops-bot: incident-log: EMBED-THRUPUT-REG-20240611 created by tyler_eng at 2024-06-11T10:02:04Z.

jamie_infra: I'll schedule the hotfix revert patch for today. Leaving notes in the ticket about kvcache sim harness and regression bench.

maria_support: thanks everyone. Closing loop with customer now.

tyler_eng: add to postmortem: include the sample_rate config in the canary checklist and capture vectors/sec baselines for embeddings workloads.

simon_ml: noted. Also adding a small synthetic that mimics tiny-doc heavy traffic to our CI harness.

maria_support: closing thread — will update if customer reopens. :white_check_mark:
